screenSummary.playArea: The scope shows input voltage. The spectrum shows the voltage in each frequency bin.
screenSummary.controlArea: Change the signal, noise, record length, averages, and detection bandwidth.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Reveal the hidden signal, then try a longer record or narrow the detection band.

signalAndNoise.currentDetails: The signal is at {{frequency}} hertz. Signal RMS is {{signal}} volts and noise RMS is {{noise}} volts.

controls.bandwidthHelp: Includes white and 1/f noise density at the signal frequency.

signalAndNoise.scope: Triggered input waveform, in volts against milliseconds.
signalAndNoise.spectrum: Input magnitude in decibel volts against log frequency.

screenSummary.playArea: Four aligned plots show the input, reference, product, and filtered output. The strip chart shows how X changes over time.
screenSummary.controlArea: Change the reference phase, frequency, or waveform and the low-pass filter settings.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Unlock the reference and change its frequency by one hertz to see a beat in X.

mixing.currentDetails: The reference is at {{frequency}} hertz, phase {{phase}} degrees. X reads {{output}} volts.
mixing.strip: Ten seconds of filtered X in volts. The latest samples appear at the right.
mixing.scope: {{stage}} waveform. Time is shared across the four plots.
mixing.spectrum: {{stage}} spectrum. Frequency is shared across the four plots.

screenSummary.playArea: The strip chart and histogram share a voltage axis. Below them, compare filter gain and measured noise.
screenSummary.controlArea: Adjust the filter, amplitude and noise. Step the signal or record a measurement.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Increase the time constant tenfold. Compare the noise band and settling time. Record several settings to trace a noise curve.

filtering.currentDetails: Time constant {{tau}} milliseconds. Filter order {{order}}. Predicted noise {{sigma}} millivolts. {{count}} recorded measurements.
filtering.strip: History of X. Shading represents measured mean plus or minus one standard deviation. A dashed line shows the predicted mean, with thin lines at one predicted standard deviation on each side.
filtering.histogram: Distribution of X. Horizontal bars show the percentage of samples in voltage bins. A Gaussian curve shows the predicted distribution.
filtering.bode: Filter gain in decibels against log frequency. The half-power point is marked. The inset shows a unit-height bandwidth rectangle with the same area as the power response on linear axes.
filtering.scaling: Measured standard deviation against time constant on log axes. Each colored line predicts the noise for one filter order.

controls.step: Step the signal from zero to the selected amplitude
controls.speedHelp: Fast runs the simulation at ten times normal speed.

screenSummary.playArea: The phasor plane and strip chart show the detected signal.
screenSummary.controlArea: Change the signal, reference phase, detuning and filter. Switch between single and dual detection.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Turn the reference phase until X is near zero, then select Auto Phase. In dual mode, watch the magnitude as you turn the knob.

phase.currentDetails: Dual mode. X {{x}} millivolts, Y {{y}} millivolts, magnitude {{r}} millivolts, angle {{theta}} degrees.
phase.plane: Equal-scale voltage axes. A trail fades over three seconds. In dual mode, the arrow and its projections show the output magnitude, phase and quadratures.
phase.strip: History of output voltage. Dual mode displays X, Y and magnitude. Single mode displays X.

controls.knobHelp: Arrow keys turn one degree. Page Up and Page Down turn fifteen degrees.
controls.detune: Detune, signal frequency minus reference frequency

screenSummary.playArea: A bench instrument measures a signal from one of three experiments. A scope shows the raw input and a notebook stores measurements.
screenSummary.controlArea: Use the rotary controls to set the amplifier. Record a reading, inspect the notebook and reveal the hidden quantities.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose an experiment, wait for the readout to settle, then press Record.

lab.reading: Reference {{frequency}} hertz. X {{x}} volts and Y {{y}} volts.
lab.unlock: Reference unlocked. Outputs are invalid during relock.
lab.inputOverload: Input overload. Samples above the input range are clipped.
lab.outputOverload: Output overload. The magnitude of X exceeds sensitivity.
lab.scope: Unclipped input in volts against milliseconds. Dashed lines show the clipping thresholds when they fit the plot.

controls.knobHelp: Drag around the dial. Arrow keys turn it and Shift plus arrow keys make finer adjustments on continuous dials.
controls.frequencyHelp: The internal reference is logarithmic. Page Up and Page Down make coarse adjustments. Hold Shift with an arrow key for fine adjustments.
controls.noiseHelp: Choose a noise level to see when voltage peaks overload the selected input range.

controls.identity: sin a · sin b = ½[cos(a−b) − cos(a+b)]
controls.harmonicNote: At 3f, the square reference has ⅓ of its fundamental gain.
controls.noiseNote: Mains adds lines at 60 Hz and 180 Hz.

filtering.powerArea: The shaded rectangle has the same area as |H(f)|².
filtering.tradeoff: 10× longer τ gives √10× less noise and 10× slower settling. A steeper slope also reduces noise and slows settling.
filtering.predictedKey: Guide lines: predicted A and A ± σ

phase.detuneNote: With detune, the phasor turns at Δf revolutions per second. R stays nearly steady through each turn.
phase.singleNote: Only X is measured. Turn θ by 90° from alignment to bring X to zero.

lab.noRows: Set the instrument, let it settle, then press RECORD.
lab.revealWaiting: Collect usable rows to compare with the hidden values.
lab.lightHint: Try 119 Hz and a 0.03 s time constant. Room-light flicker near 120 Hz creates beats. At 2f the chopped LED contributes zero.
lab.bridgeHint: At θ = 0, strain appears in X and stray capacitance mainly in Y. Use low noise and adjust both trims to null the bridge.
lab.rcHint: Sweep fᵣ and record each settled point. On the response plot, Θ = −45° at the cutoff when θ = 0.
lab.lightReveal: Divide the 1f amplitude by 2/π for absolute light levels. This factor cancels in sample-to-open-beam ratios.
lab.bridgeReveal: The closest-to-null row estimates strain and stray C from the trim settings. A null is more precise than reading X and Y directly.
lab.rcReveal: The estimate uses the recorded points around −45° with the reference phase removed.
